headline_marked: Gas crisis in Jamalpur: [[CNG auto-rickshaw fares double]]
headline: Gas crisis in Jamalpur: CNG auto-rickshaw fares double
summary: A severe gas shortage in Jamalpur has left filling stations empty, forcing drivers to hike fares and leaving commuters struggling.
details: A severe gas shortage in Jamalpur has caused a sharp decline in the number of CNG-run auto-rickshaws on the roads, leading to a surge in fares across several routes.
Drivers report waiting in queues for two to three days at filling stations, often failing to receive sufficient gas even after long waits.
On the Sarishabari-Jamalpur route, fares have jumped from Tk 50-60 to double that amount. Similarly, the Jamalpur-Bakshiganj route has seen fares rise from Tk 100-110 to Tk 200-220.
Passengers, including residents of Sarishabari, have expressed frustration, stating that the high costs are unaffordable for low-income people and calling for administrative intervention.
Jamalpur Titas Gas Manager Durjoy Khokshi stated that the main line supply was suspended since Wednesday night due to a national grid problem, though he hopes for a quick resolution.
Local authorities, including the Superintendent of Police and the Assistant Land Officer, have announced that mobile courts will be deployed to address illegal fare hikes.
caption:
CNG fares in Jamalpur have doubled as a severe gas shortage leaves drivers stranded and passengers struggling.

A severe gas shortage in Jamalpur has caused a sharp decline in the number of CNG-run auto-rickshaws on the roads, leading to a surge in fares across several routes.

Drivers report waiting in queues for two to three days at filling stations, often failing to receive sufficient gas even after long waits.

On the Sarishabari-Jamalpur route, fares have jumped from Tk 50-60 to double that amount. Similarly, the Jamalpur-Bakshiganj route has seen fares rise from Tk 100-110 to Tk 200-220.

Passengers, including residents of Sarishabari, have expressed frustration, stating that the high costs are unaffordable for low-income people and calling for administrative intervention.

Jamalpur Titas Gas Manager Durjoy Khokshi stated that the main line supply was suspended since Wednesday night due to a national grid problem, though he hopes for a quick resolution.

Local authorities, including the Superintendent of Police and the Assistant Land Officer, have announced that mobile courts will be deployed to address illegal fare hikes.

headline_marked: 908 deaths as [[measles outbreak worsens]] in Bangladesh
headline: 908 deaths as measles outbreak worsens in Bangladesh
summary: Six more suspected measles deaths were reported in 24 hours, bringing the total count to 908 this year.
details: Six patients died with measles-like symptoms in 24 hours, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
This brings the country's combined tally of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 908 for the year.
Of these fatalities, 809 are classified as suspected deaths and 99 are laboratory-confirmed.
In the same 24-hour period, 1,021 new suspected cases were reported, raising the cumulative number of suspected cases to 142,797.
Additionally, 80 new confirmed measles cases were recorded, bringing the total number of laboratory-confirmed infections to 17,880.
Since March 15, a total of 124,457 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalised across the country.
According to DGHS data, 119,939 of those hospitalised patients have recovered.
